clue.text: Following steamship covered in fuel — it's very old and rocky

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references (ff)

indicators.note: the steamship is covered in the fuel, so its letters sit inside the word for fuel

parts.note: oil is a fuel
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, as in SS Great Britain

explanation.surface: An old steamship coated in fuel oil is a relic sitting on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the ancient remains of a creature preserved in rock, so it is literally old and stony.

clue.text: Uplifting celebrations to suppress time in POW camp

indicators.note: the reversed word holds down the letter for time inside itself
in a down clue, uplifting means the word is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: galas are celebrations

explanation.surface: Cheerful festivities are banned in a prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.walkthrough: GALAS read upwards gives SALAG, and T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prison camp for captured enlisted soldiers in the Second World War.

clue.text: Star Trek character slightly upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a tad means slightly

explanation.surface: A Star Trek crew member is a bit put out.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAD turned over gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Data is the android officer in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

clue.text: Average American falls down in a quarter of North African cities

definitions.text: a quarter of North African cities

indicators.note: the letter for American drops lower in the word, which in a down entry means further along it

parts.note: the median is a kind of average

explanation.surface: An ordinary American takes a tumble in a North African city's old district.
explanation.walkthrough: In MEDIAN the A falls one place down the column, past the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The medina is the old walled native quarter found in many North African cities, as in Marrakesh or Tunis.

clue.text: Ball in from the wing leading to save that goes onto both posts

parts.note: in football a cross is a ball played in from the wing
save and bar both mean except, as in 'all save one'

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a cross leads to a save, then hits the woodwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a goalkeeper's stop, but here it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbar is the horizontal beam of a goal, fixed across the tops of the two uprights.

clue.text: Snooping around home with doctor, getting rid of damp

indicators.note: the word for snooping goes around the other letters

parts.note: spying means snooping
in means at home

explanation.surface: A nosy person poking around the house with a doctor finds damp to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin-drying removes water from wet laundry by spinning it fast in a drum.

clue.text: Amis, peut-être, avec despot

parts.note: Amis, perhaps: the novelist Martin Amis; peut-être is French for perhaps
avec is French for with; with can mean and, which in French is et

explanation.surface: French-flavoured: friends, perhaps, along with a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amis' reads as French for friends, but it is the novelist Martin Amis.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian who demands absolute obedience, close to a petty tyrant.

clue.text: I agree present has been picked up repeatedly

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word comes through by its sound
repeatedly says the sound-alike word is given twice over

parts.note: here means present, as when answering a roll call; repeatedly asks for it twice

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a gift was collected time and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Hear hear is the cry of assent from MPs and audiences backing a speaker's point.

clue.text: Agitated cat stuck in tree with last bit of stale biscuit

indicators.note: the mixed letters are stuck inside the tree

parts.note: an oak is a tree

indicators.note: an agitated cat is stirred up, so its letters are mixed
only the final letter of stale is used

explanation.surface: A frightened cat stuck up a tree, alongside a stale biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a thin, crisp Scottish biscuit made from oatmeal.

clue.text: Put back an inverted spike

indicators.note: the word for an is turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: per means a or an, as in '50p per item'
to spike a drink is to lace it

explanation.surface: Someone restores a spike that had been turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to return it to its original position.

clue.text: Plans extremely sexy retro dance with origin in Ilford

indicators.note: only the extremes, first and last letters, of sexy
retro means backward-looking, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ball is a dance

indicators.note: the origin of Ilford is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone plans a provocative throwback dance night in Ilford, an East London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabi are outlines of the topics of courses of study, so plans for teaching.

clue.text: Politician is not arse, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that a politician is, against expectations, not a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected legislator in the US and elsewhere.

clue.text: Dish made from interlocking pieces mostly served in lit brandy

parts.note: Lego is the toy of interlocking plastic bricks

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: flambé describes food served with brandy set alight

explanation.surface: A dish built from toy bricks, served in flaming brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg of lamb is a roasting joint, a classic main course.

clue.text: Lot of panic changes centre of attention

indicators.note: changes says these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A great deal of panic shifts where everyone is looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A focal point is the thing on which interest or attention is concentrated.

clue.text: Most peculiar, abandoning two good women in field

indicators.note: abandoning says these letters are removed

parts.note: strangest means most peculiar
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good woman; two of them gives two STs

explanation.surface: The oddest thing: someone leaving two virtuous women out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: One ST comes off each end of STRANGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is the scope or extent of something, as a field of activity is.

clue.text: Half of needle hidden in backpack to provide retribution

indicators.note: the half-needle is tucked inside the reversed word

parts.note: read as back pack: pack written back to front

indicators.note: half of the six-letter needle is kept, its second half dropped

explanation.surface: A needle is stashed in a backpack as an act of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backpack' looks like one bag, but it is read as two words: 'back' tells you to write 'pack' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneecap is to shoot someone in the knee as a punishment, a paramilitary act of retribution.

clue.text: Bribe to stop advocate

parts.note: to kick a habit is to stop it
to back someone is to advocate for them

explanation.surface: A bribe is offered to halt a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickback is an illicit payment made to someone for facilitating a deal.

clue.text: Hates men being confused over sex that is satisfactory

indicators.note: confused men have their letters jumbled

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
S stands for satisfactory as a grade

explanation.surface: Muddled men put sex above everything, which seems fine to them, and earn loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmities are feelings of hostility; as a plural noun it matches hates used as a noun.

clue.text: Jumble sale spreading sheer joy

indicators.note: the word for sheer spreads out around the mixed letters

parts.note: sheer means pure, as in sheer luck

indicators.note: jumble means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A jumble sale, a British charity sale of second-hand goods, spreads pure happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a feeling of happy satisfaction or enjoyment.

clue.text: Register to install independent party

indicators.note: the letter is installed inside the word for register

parts.note: a roster is a register or list of names

explanation.surface: An instruction to put an independent party on the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a political party noun, but it is the verb, to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, as at a boisterous celebration.

clue.text: Arrived with large animal

parts.note: came means arrived
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with a big creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert mammal used for transport.

clue.text: Stretched out and let go end of rope

indicators.note: only the final letter of rope is used
out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone pulled a rope taut and then released its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretched out' reads as the definition, but 'out' is the anagram signal and the definition is just 'Stretched'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongated means made longer, drawn out in length.

clue.text: Prompt brief mention in performance

indicators.note: in performance the letters are acted out in a new arrangement
brief means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A short name-check during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: MENTION loses its last letter to give MENTIO, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on time is being punctual, which is what prompt means.

clue.text: Downing drink, eat up stew

indicators.note: downing means swallowing, so the reversed word takes the drink inside it
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Knock back a drink, then finish your casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downing drink' reads as a drinking instruction, but 'Downing' says one piece swallows the other; 'up' turns the word around in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew, named after its conical pot.

clue.text: "The capital of UAE is Riyadh", Miles snarled, leaving close to apoplexy

indicators.note: snarled means tangled, so the letters are mixed
leaving says a letter is left out of the mix
the close of apoplexy is its last letter

explanation.surface: A man called Miles growls a geography mistake, nearly having a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: RIYADH plus M, without Y, is rearranged. 'capital' is money, not a city; the quoted howler about Riyadh, which is Saudi Arabia's capital, is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The dirham is the currency of the United Arab Emirates, and capital can mean money.

clue.text: Pantomime character regularly taking in victims

indicators.note: the word for victims takes the other word in, around it

parts.note: butts are victims, as in the butt of a joke
on means regularly, as when someone is on a medication they take it every day

explanation.surface: A pantomime figure who keeps picking on hapless victims.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; Buttons is the cheerful servant in Cinderella.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is a stock pantomime role, the page boy who loves Cinderella.

clue.text: Bird found in a boring Moroccan city I dispatched

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the letter goes inside
dispatched means sent away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Tangier is a port city in northern Morocco

explanation.surface: A bird spotted in a dull Moroccan city that I left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanager is a brightly coloured American songbird.

clue.text: Standard in London or Manchester

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside these words

explanation.surface: Something is the usual practice in either of two English cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a usual standard or pattern of behaviour.

clue.text: Char piece of chicken with less fat

indicators.note: a piece here is just the first letter of chicken

parts.note: leaner means having less fat

explanation.surface: Grill a cut of chicken that has less fat on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a cooking verb, but it is a British word for a charwoman, a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A char, short for charwoman, is a woman employed to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: Sitcom in which mad criminal seizes country

indicators.note: the mixed letters seize the country, holding it inside
criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A TV comedy where a crazed lawbreaker takes over a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is the BBC sitcom written by and starring Miranda Hart.
